topic.angle: Index funds replicate an index; low costs

card.title: An index fund copies a list

body.claim: An index fund doesn't pick stocks. It holds what an index holds, in the same proportions.
body.why: The aim is to match an index's performance, before fees and expenses, so there is no manager hunting for winners. Because the target index is a known quantity, it costs less to run than an actively managed fund. Fees still matter, since they are taken from what the fund earns.
